static_traits.name: Zhang Wei
static_traits.social_status: Tense, estranged relationship with colleagues due to worries about spelling errors; has a few friends but has not yet shared related anxiety with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy; sleep disturbance from anxiety in the past six months
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative; able to review trigger situations and feelings concretely; tense emotions, marked anxiety; catastrophic, future-predicting, and overgeneralizing thinking

basic_info.main_problem: I feel intense anxiety and fear about my spelling ability, believing I am a terrible speller, and worrying this will get me fired.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because fear and anxiety about spelling have started affecting my work performance and overall well-being.
growth_experiences: Long lacked confidence in spelling ability during school years, accompanied by worries about others' judgment; despite long-standing trouble, never received counseling or treatment.

core_beliefs: Mistakes will bring serious consequences (e.g. being fired)

special_situations.event: Before needing to send formal emails or conduct written communication at work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If spelling errors appear in my writing, my boss will think me unprofessional and eventually fire me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly using spell check and proofreading many times to avoid errors as much as possible
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Any small mistake could cost me my job

special_situations.event: After a colleague pointed out six months ago that there was a spelling error in my email to the boss
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Once others discover my errors, they will keep focusing on them and negate me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeping distance from coworkers, reducing communication to avoid exposing my inadequacy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They'll keep staring at my mistakes and look down on me

special_situations.event: When receiving negative feedback from colleagues about my spelling
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Being negatively evaluated means I am incompetent and will be fired sooner or later
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Further avoiding written tasks or delaying sending until repeated checking leaves nothing left to change
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am incompetent; something will go wrong sooner or later

special_situations.event: When needing to write any formal update or small note
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as it is formal writing, I will inevitably make mistakes
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Constantly checking and changing text, costing lots of time
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am bound to miss some mistake

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be recognized as competent, treated fairly, and not judged for small mistakes
core_conflict.fear: Fears being criticized, rejected, and fired, worrying about losing the job and sense of worth
defense_goal: Lowering risk through excessive proofreading and avoiding socializing, maintaining safety and a sense of control

object_relations.self_representation: Mistake-prone employee who will be negated
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh scrutinizer (a boss who might fire him)
Critical critics (colleagues who will stare at mistakes)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes a more balanced alternative viewpoint and invites examination of supporting evidence and counter-evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client tends to believe letting their guard down will bring serious consequences, feeling the counselor underestimates the risk (transference: bringing real-life anxiety and catastrophic expectations into the counseling relationship)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Insisting on emphasizing the possibility of worst cases, anxious tone, repeatedly stressing 'this isn't realistic' 'I can't do it', avoiding acknowledging positive evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about the boss's and colleagues' reactions to mistakes while lacking direct evidence
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing others will keep staring at my mistakes and negate me (transference: projecting inner criticality onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using speculative language (e.g. 'they definitely will...'), uneasy tone, avoiding discussion of concrete evidence.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: Discusses consequences of possible mistakes and coping near the time of sending an email
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Equating small mistakes with catastrophic consequences, and using over-preparation to ease anxiety
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizing the need to constantly check and prepare, listing detailed steps to lower risk, cautious and tense tone.

manifestations: Relationships with colleagues grow distant from worry about mistakes
Not yet sharing spelling-related �� anxiety and fears with friends
outcomes: Social withdrawal and growing sense of isolation

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'. Language manifestations include: 'It is all my fault that he was hurt', 'I do not deserve to talk to him', and so on
manifestations: Frequent self-reproach (such as 'I am a terrible speller')
Before sending any email, repeatedly checks and proofreads
Keeps distance from colleagues for fear of judgment

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Treating 'can't make mistakes / must write perfectly' as absolute standards
Internalizes one instance of a colleague pointing out a mistake into persistent self-regulation and vigilance

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on
manifestations: Believing the boss will look down on or fire me (lacking direct evidence)
Speculating that colleagues will keep staring at my mistakes and negate me

exception_events.target_problem: When written communication is needed (e.g. sending work emails), the client typically catastrophizes and predicts the worst, thus feeling intense anxiety, repeatedly proofreading, avoiding, and delaying.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Once a small spelling error appeared in a work email; colleagues just corrected it and continued working, no criticism or follow-up from the boss, the incident quickly passed.
exception_events.reason: Different support/situation: colleagues oriented to correcting and continuing work, didn't magnify the error; real feedback showing small mistakes don't yet bring serious consequences.

positive_force: Able to use strategies like spell check and repeated proofreading
Willing to proactively seek counseling help
Still retains passion for dance work
Having a few friends to talk with (though not yet sharing this anxiety)
negative_force: Cognitive patterns of catastrophizing, predicting the future, and overgeneralization
Persistent anxiety and sleep disturbance affecting function
Excessive self-blame and self-monitoring, worrying about others' evaluation
Social avoidance causing decreased support at work
Damaged self-identity ('I am a terrible speller')

target_behavior.behavior: Intense anxiety and compulsive repeated proofreading before work written communication
antecedent: Needing to send emails or formal written materials
Realizing colleagues once pointed out spelling mistakes
Receiving or anticipating negative feedback on spelling
target_behavior.core_reason: Long-standing lack of spelling confidence and fear of being judged; catastrophizing small mistakes and predicting being fired
target_behavior.function: Avoids potential negative evaluation or punishment, gaining short-term safety and a sense of control
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased work efficiency and impaired performance; anxiety maintained; sleep disturbance and decreased attention

target_behavior.behavior: Social avoidance and estrangement at work
antecedent: Worrying that colleagues or supervisors will notice one's spelling errors
Needing to discuss written content or emails with colleagues
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing others' judgment, overgeneralizing one mistake into sustained negation
target_behavior.function: Escapes criticism and shame; maintains surface safety
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with colleagues, decreased support, worsening isolation, further worsening anxiety and work performance
